name: Vivienne
classification_notes: A display face built around fluid, overlapping strokes and deliberately compromised legibility, named after Vivienne Westwood.
summary: A fluid, layered display face named after Vivienne Westwood, built to worry at the edge of legibility rather than sit comfortably inside it.
description: Vivienne leans on movement and overlapping strokes, letting lace-like layers and confusion weave between letters instead of settling into a clean, readable structure. It was recognised at the 10th Bienal de Tipografía Latinoamericana Tipos Latinos.
foundry_blurb: Fer Cozzi describes Vivienne as inspired by movement, fluid strokes and the challenge of legibility within every structure, with layers and lace navigating the rigid boundaries of typographic convention.

name: Aidé
classification_notes: A display face with super-thin serifs and sharply pointed stems, inspired directly by a hedgehog, classified as display given its headline-scale intent.
summary: A prickly, hedgehog-inspired display face where open round shapes merge with super-thin serifs for a spiked texture.
description: Aidé combines sharp-pointed vertical stems with extra-long, delicate serifs, producing a fractured look balanced by an elegant, spiky finish. Its Cyrillic was developed with feedback from Krista Radoeva, and it won the Latin category at the 10th Founder Type Design Competition.
foundry_blurb: Fer Cozzi describes Aidé as a prickly yet sweet display typeface where open and round shapes merge with super-thin serifs, blending spheres and spines into a delicate yet strong system.

name: June Expt
classification_notes: A variable display face built around two named extremes, Active and Curious, rather than a conventional weight axis, named for virologist June Almeida.
summary: A variable display face built between two named extremes, Active and Curious, named for coronavirus-imaging pioneer June Almeida.
description: June Expt is designed around two contrasting poles: Curious, an exploratory and risk-taking form, and Active, a more structured and methodical one, with the variable axis moving between them. It's available as Active, Curious, a complete set, or the full variable font.
foundry_blurb: Fer Cozzi and Oscar Guerrero describe June as merging two contrasting design philosophies into a complex system of different flavour and texture, with two extremes and everything in between.

name: Tomasa
classification_notes: A display face built from four structural variants per letter, drawing directly on graffiti and street-tagging letterforms rather than any formal type tradition.
summary: A graffiti-rooted display face with four structural variants per letter, named for Chilean singer Tomasa del Real.
description: Tomasa interprets the letterforms of street art and tagging, offering four variants of each character to capture the rhythm of rap, hip hop and trap. It won the 10th Founder Type Design Competition and Chile's Sello Buen Diseño, and made Typographica's Favourites of 2019.
foundry_blurb: Fer Cozzi describes Tomasa as rooted in the visual and musical urban subcultures, its formal explorations interpreting the letterforms found in street art and celebrating the peculiarities of graffiti and urban tagging.

name: Inge
classification_notes: A single-weight, narrow display face named for seismologist Inge Lehmann, classified as display for its large-scale, solid-block intended use.
summary: A tight, narrow display face in three angles, upright, backslanted and slanted, named for seismologist Inge Lehmann.
description: Inge's narrow, single-weight shapes suit large-scale, solid blocks of text, with the side-to-side movement across its three angle variants hinting at acceleration without losing control.
foundry_blurb: Fer Cozzi describes Inge as a tight display font with a strong sense of rhythm and a solid texture, its narrow shapes ideal for large-scale use and robust, solid text blocks.

name: Gabriella
classification_notes: A single, super-heavy weight display face with extreme, wide shapes, classified as display for its headline-only intended use.
summary: A wide, super-heavy display face with extreme shapes, named after the Little Mermaid character to celebrate inclusiveness in type design.
description: Gabriella pushes width and weight to their limits, aiming for a design that makes a message unmissable rather than quietly legible. It won recognition at the 10th Founder Type Design Competition.
foundry_blurb: Fer Cozzi describes Gabriella as a wide, emotional and striking typeface with extreme shapes and a super heavy weight, full of character and a special charm.

name: Rosalind
classification_notes: A modular display face built from a deconstructed set of shapes recombined into letterforms, named for DNA researcher Rosalind Franklin.
summary: A modular display face built from a deconstructed set of basic shapes, named for DNA researcher Rosalind Franklin.
description: Rosalind breaks each letter down into a small set of modules and recombines them, producing multiple possible forms per character through a playful, systematic process rather than a fixed drawing.
foundry_blurb: Fer Cozzi describes Rosalind as a modular typeface built from a basic set of shapes, designed through a playful and experimental process where letters are deconstructed into modules and recombined.

name: Síncopa
classification_notes: A high-contrast, eclectic display face named for musical syncopation, offered in three variants each inspired by a different jazz singer.
summary: A high-contrast display face named for musical syncopation, its three variants each channelling a different jazz singer.
description: Síncopa plays stability against dynamism through its three variants, Billie, Nina and Ella, each carrying stylistic alternates that push its contrasting strokes and eclectic letterforms in a different direction.
foundry_blurb: Fer Cozzi describes Síncopa as inspired by three queens of jazz, Billie, Nina and Ella, emulating their bold voices and distinctive personalities through highly contrasting strokes and eclectic letterforms.
